sentences.text:
JUDGMENT "Whether the compensation awarded to the appellant under the impugned award is just"? is the question involved in this case.
2.
The appellant was the claimant and respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the respondents in M.V.C.No.288/2019 before the Tribunal.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to according to their ranks before the Tribunal.

3. On 23.11.2018 at about 11.00 a.m. when the claimant was proceeding on his scooter bearing registration No.KA-20-V-3280 near Uchila Pete, Bada Village within the limits of Padubidri Police Station, goods lorry bearing No.KA-01-D-8464 hit him causing the accident.
The claimant suffered grievous injuries.

Between 23.11.2018 till 15.12.2018, he was treated as inpatient in KMC Hospital,
Manipal.
His right leg was amputed below knee.

At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and Insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-D-8464.
4.

The claimant filed M.V.C.No.288/2019 before the Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT,
Karkala against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.35,33,666/- on the ground that due to the accident and consequential injuries, he has suffered permanent physical disability and loss of future earnings.

entities.text:
Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT,
Karkala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He claimed that the respondents are liable to compensate him.
5. Respondent No.1 did not contest the petition.

Respondent No.2 contested the petition denying actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, age, occupation, income, disability of the claimant and its liability to pay the compensation.
6. The Tribunal on recording the evidence and on hearing the parties by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry by its driver.

The Tribunal relying on the evidence of PW.2 the doctor and other evidence on record held that the claimant has suffered 70% disability to his right lower limb and assessed the same to the whole body at 23%.
The Tribunal considered the income of the claimant at 10,000/- per month, his age at 45 years awarded total compensation of Rs.5,98,270/- on different heads as per the table below.

sentences.text: To prove amputation of leg and permanent physical disability the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the doctor PW2 who treated him.
As per the evidence of PW.2, the claimant has suffered open segmental fracture of right tibia with vascular injury.

His period of hospitalization and treatment for the said injury as per the evidence of PW.2 are as follows:
1. Admission on 23.11.2018 2. CTVS consultations 3.
Right below knee amputation done on 23.11.2018 4. Right knee disarticulation, revision amputation done on 27.11.2018 5. Discharged on 03.12.2018 6.

The above evidence goes to show that the claimant was treated as inpatient in Kasturba Hospital,
Manipal between 23.11.2018 to 03.12.2018 and he underwent amputation of right limb on 27.11.2018.

As per the evidence of PW.2, the details of the amputation are as follows:
"Right below knee amputation stump (10 cm from the knee joint line)"
11.
As per the evidence of PW.2, permanent physical disability of the claimant was 70% to the right lower limb.
Neither he spoke about what was the disability to whole body nor the claimant's Counsel elicited that in the evidence.
Therefore permanent physical disability of the claimant to the whole body has to be taken at 1/3rd of the disability spoken by PW.2.
Therefore the Tribunal considered the same at 23%.
However, that can be rounded to 25%.
12. According to the claimant, he was working as Cook which requires major involvement of the upper limbs.
Therefore the contention that such injury has caused 100% functional disability to the claimant cannot be accepted.
Perusal of the judgment relied on by learned Counsel for the claimant shows that in all those cases, the victim were either driver/agriculturist.
Therefore it was held that loss of lower limb causes major permanent physical disability to the said claimants.
Whereas in case of cook, as already pointed out, upper limb of the body needs major movement.
Suffice to say that the said judgments are not applicable to the facts of this case.
13. Regarding occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the goods lorry, the parties are not at issue.
As per the claimant himself, at the time of the accident, he was aged 45 years and was employed as Cook in Mahalaxmi Hotel and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To substantiate that contention, except self serving statement, no other evidence was led.

Needless to Suresh Kulal vs Girish B D on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171017350/

sentences.text: Therefore income of the claimant has to be assessed notionally.
14. The accident occurred in the year 2018.

Having regard to the nature of the work of the claimant,
the cost of living and prevailing wage rates during the said period, the Tribunal should have considered his income at Rs.12,500/- per month.

15. Having regard to the age of the claimant and the fact that he was working as cook, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi8 25% has to be super added to the income of the claimant by way of future AIR 2017 SC 5157 prospects which comes to Rs.12,500/- + 3125=15,625/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering permanent physical disability at 25%, loss of monthly income comes to Rs.15,625 x 25/100 = 3906.25 rounded to Rs.3,906/-.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation9 the applicable multiplier is 13.

entities.text: Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore compensation payable on the head of loss of future earnings comes to Rs.3906 x 12 x 13= Rs.6,09,336/-.
16.
The compensation awarded on the head of medical expenses is based on the documents produced.
Therefore that needs to be maintained.

Having regard to the disability suffered by the claimant, his evidence and the medical evidence, the compensation awarded on the head of pain and sufferings and loss of amenities is on the lower side.
The Tribunal should have awarded compensation at Rs.1,00,000/- each on both heads.
17. The compensation payable on the head of loss of income during laid up period comes to 12,500 x 3 = Rs.37,500/-.
The compensation awarded on the head of future medical expenses i.e. for purchasing artificial limb AIR 2009 SC 3104 - 10 - was based on the documents produced by the claimant.
Therefore that needs no interference.
On the head of attendant charges, diet and transportation it is just to award, global compensation of Rs.15,000/-.

Therefore the just compensation payable is as follows:
